svg.text: Eave section, roof-to-wall junction
Printed pieces: inner leaf / filled lattice / skin · Ishigaki · 1:10 at A3 · cm
Roof inner leaf, printed reinforced concrete, 24 at the ring beam
tapering to 8 (one bead) at the top of the 8 m roof; bars in printed
holes stop at 9 (z ≈ 7.5 m)
Ring beam 24 × 30 on the wall inner leaf, cast in place, 4 Ø16,
stirrups Ø8 / 150; ties the roof's outward push
Starter bars Ø12 from the ring beam into the roof leaf, lap 650
Printed lattice 150 (your idea): one 20 mm zig-zag bead at ≈ 20°,
touching each leaf every ≈ 80 cm (see plan); cells filled with cork
granulate or water-repellent perlite (λ ≈ 0.05); U ≈ 0.47
Breathable water-repellent mineral coating on all outside faces
(moisture control on the outside in a cooled building)
Roof outer skin 80, printed with the lattice and inner leaf as one
piece; stainless wire in bed joints; light colour
Printed drip nose 2⁵ on the bottom roof course, so rain drips clear of
the wall; no gutter
Wall inner leaf, reinforced concrete 240, mesh both faces
Wall lattice 150, same as (4)
Wall outer skin 80, same as (6)
Fill runs on from the wall lattice into the roof lattice: no gap in
the insulation at the eave; cap it at the top opening
Room-side face: printed concrete, pitch 63.4° (course 300, step 150
from the roof script)
from scripts/cork_house_roof.py or given by you
assumed by me: not defined yet
Notes
Each piece = inner leaf + lattice + outer skin, printed in one go, open top/bottom.
Ribs are the heat bridges: few, long, flat ribs (≈ 20°) keep U ≈ 0.47. Empty cells ≈ 2.0.
Inner leaf 24 → 8 (load ≈ 0.3 MPa at the base). Widths horizontal, as printed.
Hand estimates, not engineered or simulated: confirm structure + U-value.
